newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GPA net profit $54 mln in yr to March 31.
newsitem.headline: GPA net profit $54 mln in yr to March 31.

text.p: Irish-based aircraft leasing firm GPA Group Plc said on Tuesday it made a net profit of $54 million in the year to end-March 1996 versus a net loss of $26 million the previous year.

GPA said a number of exceptional gains in the final quarter of the financial year had affected the results. The company made an exceptional net gain of $34 million on a major restructuring deal and a gain of $18 million on the sale of securities in two U.S. airlines, GPA said in a statement.
It said the highlight of the year had been the completion of the restructuring, which involved the securitised sale of 229 aircraft and related assets to Airplanes Group for $4.6 billion.
"The focus of our activities during the year was the completion of our restructuring," chief executive Patrick Blaney said in a statement.
"The success of these efforts has strengthened GPA's financial position considerably," he said.

GPA said revenue in the year to end-March was $1.135 billion versus $1.617 billion the previous year. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation came to $664 million versus $648 million.
Net interest expense over the year was $324 million versus $379 million, and cash inflow from operating activities was $559 million versus $1.138 billion, GPA said.
"The core leasing business during the year was markedly better with number of non-revenue earning aircraft at a low level and the cost of lessee defaults reducing," Blaney said.
"Lease rates continued to improve as demand for aircraft hardened."
He said that if these trends continued they would result in new leases at higher rates and so contribute to an improved performance over time.
"GPA's results for the year to March 31, 1997, however, will reflect the much reduced number of aircraft in its portfolio following the sales to Airplanes Group," Blaney said.

Shareholders' funds at March 31 were $166 million versus $111 million the previous year. Borrowings were $1.575 billion versus $4.655 billion and total assets were $2.406 billion versus 6.086 billion at end-March 1995.
